Allotments reopen after the winter

The gates of the Linden Row allotments opened again on the first Saturday of March, and by mid-morning more than forty plot holders had turned up with spades, seed trays and flasks of tea. The flooded lower path has been rebuilt with a gravel surface that drains far better than the old one. The work was paid for by the spring fair and carried out by volunteers over six weekends. Seven plots are still free, and anyone who lives in the parish can apply for one. Half plots are available for newcomers who would like to try growing vegetables
There is no charge, although donations towards spare parts are always welcome.

Meet the new warden

Priya Hollingworth started as our community warden in January. She grew up two streets away from Linden Row and spent eight years working for a housing charity in the city. Priya will be at the community centre every Tuesday morning for anyone who wants to raise a problem in person. She is especially keen to hear from older residents who feel cut off during the winter months. “I want people to know there is somebody they can simply knock on the door of,” she says. Priya can also be reached by telephone on the number printed on the back of the residents’ directory.
From the residents’ committee
At its February meeting the committee agreed the following points:
– to ask the council for a pedestrian crossing outside the primary school;
– to buy two new benches for the village green;

– to hold the summer fair on Saturday 27 June;
– to look for a new treasurer from September.
The committee meets on the first Thursday of every month at half past seven, and all residents are welcome to attend. Minutes of past meetings are kept in the folder at the library counter.
Lost and found

A child’s blue scooter was left by the bus shelter on Mill Lane in February. A set of keys on a red ribbon was handed in after the litter pick. Both can be collected from the community centre office during opening hours.
Write for the Courier

The Courier is written, edited and delivered by volunteers. We would love to hear about your club, your street or your memories of the village. Articles for the summer issue should reach the editor by 15 May, and photographs are very welcome.
